t: Uruk in southern Iraq grew into the largest city in the world in the fourth millennium BCE.
Administrators in its Eanna temple precinct produced proto-cuneiform, among the earliest known writing, around 3300 BCE.
It was the city of Gilgamesh and the capital of Lugal-zage-si before falling to Akkad, Ur and finally Larsa.
dyk: The Warka Vase and the Mask of Warka, two of Uruk’s greatest treasures, were looted from the Iraq Museum in Baghdad in 2003 and both were later recovered.
ev: Administrators in Eanna begin recording goods on clay tablets: the beginning of writing
Uruk outposts in Syria and Iran are abandoned
A city wall about 9 km long encloses Uruk
Approximate date of Gilgamesh, the city’s legendary king
Lugal-zage-si makes Uruk the capital of a united Sumer
Utu-hengal of Uruk defeats the Gutian king Tirigan
Sin-kashid founds Uruk’s last independent dynasty
